summary: Composio already provides a managed Calendly OAuth app, so you can connect users today without registering anything. Registering your own app is self-serve through a separate Calendly developer account, and I found no documented review step. The main gotcha is that Sandbox and Production are separate apps, Production needs an HTTPS redirect URI, and the client secret is shown only once.

verdict.difficultyReason: Composio supplies a managed app, and a custom app is self-serve with no documented approval or review.

devReady.estimate: 5 min with the Composio managed app; 20-40 min with your own Sandbox app
devReady.detail: Managed: create a Composio session and connect your own Calendly account. Custom: create a Sandbox OAuth app in the Calendly developer portal, then paste its Client ID and Secret into a Composio auth config. Sandbox apps are for test data, not live customer data.

productionReady.estimate: Same day (about 1 hour) as far as the docs show
productionReady.detail: Managed app: any user can connect right away, but the consent screen says Composio and quota is shared. Custom: create a separate Production app with an HTTPS redirect URI. No approval gate is documented in the pages I read. Confirm this with a real Production app.

verdict.handsOnEffort: 30-60 minutes for a custom app; near zero for managed

nextAction: Connect your own Calendly account through a Composio session with no authConfigs set, which uses the managed app. If you need your own branding, sign up at https://developer.calendly.com with GitHub or Google.

accessPaths.name: Composio managed app
accessPaths.whenToUse: Prototypes, internal tools, and anything that doesn't need your own branding.
accessPaths.limits: Consent screen shows Composio. Quota is shared across Composio users. Triggers poll at a 15-minute minimum.

accessPaths.name: Custom Calendly app (Sandbox)
accessPaths.whenToUse: Developing and testing with your own app before going live.
accessPaths.limits: Intended for test data. Localhost over HTTP is allowed as a redirect URI, though Composio's redirect is HTTPS anyway.

accessPaths.name: Custom Calendly app (Production)
accessPaths.whenToUse: Your own branding, custom scopes and separate rate limits for real customers.
accessPaths.limits: Redirect URI must be HTTPS. None else known.

prerequisites.detail: Separate from a normal Calendly user account. Sign up at developer.calendly.com with GitHub or Google.

prerequisites.item: Calendly user account to test with
prerequisites.detail: Any Calendly account works to connect through the managed app.
Needed for the dashboard and API key.

prerequisites.item: Paid or Enterprise Calendly plan (some features)
prerequisites.detail: Search results say activity_log:read needs Enterprise. This comes from a third-party summary, not an official page I read. Some API features may also depend on plan.

phases.title: Use the managed app
phases.goal: A Calendly account is connected through Composio with no registration.

steps.title: Create a session without authConfigs
steps.detail: Toolkits not listed in authConfigs keep using Composio managed auth. Start a Calendly connection and approve it with your Calendly account.

phases.title: Register your own Sandbox app (optional)
phases.goal: An OAuth flow works with your own Calendly app.

steps.title: Sign up for a developer account
steps.detail: Use GitHub or Google. It is separate from your Calendly user account.

steps.title: Create an OAuth application
steps.detail: Enter a name, choose kind Web, pick environment Sandbox, set the redirect URI to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, and select scopes.

steps.title: Save the credentials immediately
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID, Client Secret and Webhook signing key. The secret and signing key cannot be viewed again.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
steps.detail: Dashboard > Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > Calendly > OAuth2 > paste Client ID and Secret > Create. Copy the ac_... ID and pass it in authConfigs keyed by calendly.

steps.title: Connect a test account
steps.detail: Run the flow and confirm tokens come back and an API call works.

phases.title: Go live with your own app
phases.goal: Real users connect with your branding.

steps.title: Create a separate Production app
steps.detail: The docs recommend creating a new Production app rather than reusing the Sandbox one. The redirect URI must be HTTPS. Request the minimum scopes you need.

steps.title: Swap credentials in the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a new auth config with the Production Client ID and Secret, then use its ac_ ID in sessions.

steps.title: Test with a second Calendly account
steps.detail: Confirm a user outside your organization can connect, because no review is documented and I couldn't verify this.

scopes.purpose: Read the current user and organization info
List and read scheduled events and invitees

scopes.reviewNote: Reported as Enterprise-plan only by a third-party summary; not confirmed on Calendly's own page

blockers.title: New apps have no API access until scopes are granted
blockers.symptom: API calls return permission errors after connecting.
blockers.fix: Select the needed scopes on the app and have users reconnect. Existing installs may need to reauthorize to get new scopes.

blockers.title: Client secret shown only once
blockers.symptom: You can't find the secret after leaving the creation page.
blockers.fix: Copy it at creation. If lost, create a new app or rotate the secret if the portal allows it.

blockers.title: Production redirect URI must be HTTPS
blockers.symptom: Redirect URI rejected on a Production app.

blockers.title: Sandbox app used for real users
blockers.symptom: Real customers can't connect or data is test-only.
blockers.fix: Create a separate Production app and update the Composio auth config.

blockers.title: Enterprise-only scopes
blockers.symptom: Scope like activity_log:read unavailable on non-Enterprise accounts.
blockers.fix: Use an Enterprise Calendly organization, or drop the scope.

technical.pkce: S256 supported and recommended for web and native apps. Calendly does not enforce it for web apps.
technical.refreshTokens: Refresh token grant is supported, per the docs link. I could not confirm access token lifetime or rotation rules from the pages I read.
technical.redirectUriRules: Sandbox allows http://localhost. Production requires HTTPS. Use a specific redirect_uri. Number allowed and wildcard rules were not confirmed.
technical.notes: The docs say to POST the code to auth.calendly.com, but my discovery probe found the token endpoint at calendly.com/oauth/token (auth.calendly.com/oauth/authorize 301-redirects to calendly.com/oauth/authorize). The discovery document also advertises a registration_endpoint, which I did not use. Composio also has a separate calendly_mcp toolkit using dynamic client registration OAuth. A second issuer, login.calendly.com, exists and its metadata lists standard OIDC scopes, but I did not determine how it relates to the API apps.

canDo: Create Composio sessions that use the managed Calendly app
Draft the Calendly app name, description and scope list
Build the auth config and session code with authConfigs
Test the connection and API calls after you connect
youMustDo: Sign up for the Calendly developer account
Copy and store the client secret at creation
Approve consent with your Calendly login

drafts.title: Calendly OAuth app description

We request only these scopes: [SCOPES]. Data is used only to serve the requesting user and is not sold or shared. Privacy policy: [URL]. Support: [EMAIL].

sources.title: Composio: custom app vs managed app
Search summary citing third-party vendor guides on Enterprise scopes (Frontegg, Scalekit)

probes.observed: OAUTH2 is Composio-managed. Redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Default scopes empty. A separate calendly_mcp toolkit uses DCR_OAUTH.
probes.conclusion: You can connect users without your own app.

probes.observed: OIDC metadata at calendly.com: authorize /oauth/authorize, token /oauth/token, PKCE S256, auth method none, registration_endpoint present. A second issuer at login.calendly.com also responds.
probes.conclusion: Endpoints are live. PKCE S256 is supported.

probes.observed: 301 to calendly.com/oauth/authorize, then 302 to calendly.com/app/login (200). It didn't show an invalid-client error.
probes.conclusion: The endpoint is live and sends unauthenticated users to login. It doesn't validate the client before login.

probes.observed: 404 Page not found. The site mentions /llms.txt for a docs index.
probes.conclusion: That URL guess was wrong. The developer site itself is live, and my fetches of its other pages worked.

uncertainties: I found no documented app review process, but I did not log into the developer portal. A real Production app is the only way to confirm that arbitrary users can connect.
Access token lifetime and refresh token rotation weren't on the pages I read. The Calendly FAQ would cover them.
The docs say to POST to auth.calendly.com for tokens, but discovery lists calendly.com/oauth/token. Composio handles this for you.
Which scopes need a paid or Enterprise plan is only reported by a third-party summary.
Whether the Production environment limits the number of users or imposes rate limits wasn't documented in the pages I read.
I did not search for Calendly policy changes in the last 12 months beyond one search. The scope catalog (23 scopes, including newer ones like meeting_recaps and contacts) suggests recent changes.
